subject.title: fix(gateway): MCP clients receive responses for JSON-RPC notifications

question: Should Gateway MCP loopback treat every valid JSON-RPC message without an `id` as a notification, even if an existing client accidentally omitted `id` while expecting a `tools/list` or `tools/call` result?
rationale: The change is protocol-correct, but it intentionally changes the behavior of existing id-less MCP calls from `200` with a JSON result to `202` with no body, so the remaining choice is an owner compatibility decision rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Accept spec-compliant notifications
options.body: Merge this shape once real behavior proof is added, treating omitted `id` as the client choosing notification semantics.

options.title: Require a staged compatibility path
options.body: Ask for a compatibility-preserving transition if maintainers believe current id-less clients need a deprecation window or diagnostics before losing response bodies.

options.title: Pause for broader MCP transport policy
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want one coordinated policy for all raw HTTP MCP request-shape validation before accepting targeted fixes.

recommendation.title: Accept spec-compliant notifications
recommendation.body: Merge this shape once real behavior proof is added, treating omitted `id` as the client choosing notification semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and merged the current MCP loopback response aggregation surface and is the strongest current-history owner signal for this boundary.
